messages.subject: Nimble Sampler C++ Error
parts:
Hi all,

I'm taking a stab at writing a custom sampler in NIMBLE and am currently in the trouble-shooting phase. 

After running: 

mcmcbirds <- configureMCMC(prepbirds, monitors = pars, print = T, control = list(adaptInterval = adaptInterval, scale=.1))
    mcmcbirds$removeSampler(c("s", "z", "parent", "age.pre", "nFledglings"))
    mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = c("s", "z", "parent", "age.pre", "nFledglings"),
                         type = "myRWtrajectoryPotentialSampler", silent = F,
                         control = list(scale=SamplerScale, adaptInterval = adaptInterval, adaptScaleOnly = T,
                                        npix = nc$npix, pxw = nc$pxw, xmin = nc$xmin, ymin = nc$ymin, xmax = nc$xmax, ymax = nc$ymax,
                                        gcoords = nc$gcoords, pixels = nd$pixels, known.z = known.z, known.parent = known.parent,
                                        known.s = known.s, known.age = known.age, known.fledge = known.fledge, east = nd$east,
                                        north = nd$north, nocc = nc$nocc, M = nc$M, xoffset = nc$xoffset, yoffset = nc$yoffset
                                        ))
   
    birdsMCMC <- buildMCMC(mcmcbirds)
    Cmodel <- compileNimble(prepbirds) #takes a long time (sometimes)
    Compbirds <- compileNimble(birdsMCMC, project = prepbirds)

I get the message: "Error: Failed to create the shared library. Run 'printErrors()'. PrintErrors gives me:

P_22_MCMC.cpp:1144:40: error: no matching function for call to 'Rf_rpois'
  nFledge_dot_prop((i) - 1, (t) - 1) = rpois(fledge_dot_lam);
                                       ^~~~~
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/Rmath.h:333:16: note: expanded from macro 'rpois'
#define rpois           Rf_rpois
                        ^~~~~~~~
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/Rmath.h:498:8: note: candidate function not viable: no known conversion from 'NimArr<1, double>' to 'double' for 1st argument
double  rpois(double);
        ^
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/Rmath.h:333:16: note: expanded from macro 'rpois'
#define rpois           Rf_rpois
                        ^
2 warnings and 1 error generated.
make: *** [P_22_MCMC.o] Error 1

I guess this means I'm implementing the rpois function wrong somehow while making the sampler? 

Here's the relevant part of the sampler code:

nFledge.prop <- array(NA, dim = c(M, TT))

for(i in 1:M){
     for(t in 1:TT){
       fledge.lam <- exp(alpha0+alpha1*Nt[t])*sex[i]*z.prop[i,t]
       nFledge.prop[i,t] <- rpois(1, fledge.lam)
     }
    }


Any help would be appreciated!

Best,
Heather Gaya

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Nimble Sampler C++ Error
parts:
Heather, I admit offhand I don't see what's going wrong with your code.  Use of 

x <- rpois(1, lambda)

should work fine in compiled code (e.g., inside the run function of a custom-written MCMC sampler).

Is it possible for you to distill this down to a (minimal) reproducible example, which I can run to recreate the error?  If you would prefer to send that directly (off list) to avoid distributing details of your sampler or model code, that's fine as well.

Thanks,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Nimble Sampler C++ Error
parts:
Here's a simple example that has the same error:

## Nimble code: 
fakenim <- nimbleCode({
  alpha0 ~ dnorm(10, .3)
  alpha1 ~ dunif(-2, 2)

  for(i in 1:M){
    sex[i] ~ dbern(.5)
    for(t in 1:nocc){
      log(fecundity_dens[i,t]) <- alpha0+alpha1*Nt[t]
      nFledglings[i,t] ~ dpois(fecundity_dens[i,t]*sex[i])
    } #end t
  } #end i
})

### My sampler: 

myfakeSampler <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
    M <- control$M
    nocc <- control$nocc
    Nt <- control$Nt
  },
  run = function() {
    alpha0.curr <- model$alpha0
    alpha1.curr <- model$alpha1
    sex <- model$sex
    nFledge.curr <- model$nFledglings
    model_lp_initial <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)
   
    nFledge.prop <- array(NA, c(M, nocc))
   
    for(i in 1:10){
      nFledge.prop[i,1] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[1]*sex[i]))
      nFledge.prop[i,2] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[2]*sex[i]))
      nFledge.prop[i,3] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[3]*sex[i]))
    }
   
    nFledge.prop[11:50,] <- nFledge.curr[11:50,]
    model$nFledglings <<- nFledge.prop
    #model$alpha <<- alpha.prop
    model_lp_proposed <- model$calculate(calcNodes)  
    log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial
   
    accept <- decide(log_MH_ratio)
    if(accept) {
      copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    } else {
      copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    }
   
  },
  methods = list( reset = function () {} )
)


##make up some data
set.seed(10)
fakesex <- rbinom(50,1,.5)
nFledglings <- matrix(NA, nrow = 50, ncol =3)
for(i in 1:50){
nFledglings[i,1] <- rpois(1, exp(1+.5*10)*fakesex[i])
nFledglings[i,2] <- rpois(1,exp(1+.5*3)*fakesex[i])
nFledglings[i,3] <- rpois(1, exp(1+.5*5)*fakesex[i])
}
nFledglings.init <- nFledglings
nFledglings.init[11:50,] <- NA
nFledglings[1:10,] <- NA

#### run the model:

mydat <- list(sex = fakesex, nFledglings = nFledglings)
myconsts <- list(M = 50, nocc = 3, Nt = c(10, 3, 5))
inits <- list(alpha0 = 1, alpha1 = .5, nFledglings = nFledglings.init)
prepbirds <- nimbleModel(code =fakenim, constants = myconsts,
                         data = mydat, inits = inits, calculate = T, check = T) #goes fast w/ fake data :)
prepbirds$calculate()
adaptInterval = 200
SamplerScale <- 0.75
mcmcbirds <- configureMCMC(prepbirds, monitors = c("alpha0", "alpha1"), print = T, control = list(adaptInterval = adaptInterval, scale=.1))

mcmcbirds$removeSampler(c("nFledglings"))
mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = c("nFledglings"), control =  list(M = 50, nocc = 3, Nt = c(10,3,5)),
                     type = "myfakeSampler", silent = F)

Compbirds <- compileNimble(birdsMCMC, project = prepbirds) ### This throws the error
Compbirds$run(niter = 10, nburnin = 0, thin = 1, reset = F)

parts:
Per usual, as soon as I sent the smaller version to the listserv, I figured out my problem.

If I change:

to:
alpha0.curr <- model[['alpha0']]
 alpha1.curr <- model[['alpha1']] 

then the error goes away.  I would have thought both versions would produce a scalar, but somehow that was not the case.

Apologies to all for the multiple emails and thank you everyone for your patience! 


-Heather Gaya

Hi Heather, indeed the dimensionality behavior of those two syntaxes is different. It's noted in the documentation, but not all that easy to find (and I see the documentation has a typo in the key sentence about this that I'll make a note for us to fix). I don't remember off-hand why the behavior is different.

-chris
On Mon, Aug 7, 2023 at 7:29 PM heather...@gmail.com <heather...@gmail.com> wrote:

Per usual, as soon as I sent the smaller version to the listserv, I figured out my problem.

If I change:
alpha0.curr <- model$alpha0
 alpha1.curr <- model$alpha1

to:
alpha0.curr <- model[['alpha0']]
 alpha1.curr <- model[['alpha1']] 

then the error goes away.  I would have thought both versions would produce a scalar, but somehow that was not the case.

Apologies to all for the multiple emails and thank you everyone for your patience! 


-Heather Gaya

On Monday, August 7, 2023 at 7:18:21 PM UTC-4 heather...@gmail.com wrote:
Here's a simple example that has the same error:

## Nimble code: 
fakenim <- nimbleCode({
  alpha0 ~ dnorm(10, .3)
  alpha1 ~ dunif(-2, 2)

  for(i in 1:M){
    sex[i] ~ dbern(.5)
    for(t in 1:nocc){
      log(fecundity_dens[i,t]) <- alpha0+alpha1*Nt[t]
      nFledglings[i,t] ~ dpois(fecundity_dens[i,t]*sex[i])
    } #end t
  } #end i
})

### My sampler: 

myfakeSampler <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
    M <- control$M
    nocc <- control$nocc
    Nt <- control$Nt
  },
  run = function() {
    alpha0.curr <- model$alpha0
    alpha1.curr <- model$alpha1
    sex <- model$sex
    nFledge.curr <- model$nFledglings
    model_lp_initial <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)
   
    nFledge.prop <- array(NA, c(M, nocc))
   
    for(i in 1:10){
      nFledge.prop[i,1] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[1]*sex[i]))
      nFledge.prop[i,2] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[2]*sex[i]))
      nFledge.prop[i,3] <- rpois(1, exp(alpha0.curr + alpha1.curr*Nt[3]*sex[i]))
    }
   
    nFledge.prop[11:50,] <- nFledge.curr[11:50,]
    model$nFledglings <<- nFledge.prop
    #model$alpha <<- alpha.prop
    model_lp_proposed <- model$calculate(calcNodes)  
    log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial
   
    accept <- decide(log_MH_ratio)
    if(accept) {
      copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    } else {
      copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    }
   
  },
  methods = list( reset = function () {} )
)


##make up some data
set.seed(10)
fakesex <- rbinom(50,1,.5)
nFledglings <- matrix(NA, nrow = 50, ncol =3)
for(i in 1:50){
nFledglings[i,1] <- rpois(1, exp(1+.5*10)*fakesex[i])
nFledglings[i,2] <- rpois(1,exp(1+.5*3)*fakesex[i])
nFledglings[i,3] <- rpois(1, exp(1+.5*5)*fakesex[i])
}
nFledglings.init <- nFledglings
nFledglings.init[11:50,] <- NA
nFledglings[1:10,] <- NA

#### run the model:

mydat <- list(sex = fakesex, nFledglings = nFledglings)
myconsts <- list(M = 50, nocc = 3, Nt = c(10, 3, 5))
inits <- list(alpha0 = 1, alpha1 = .5, nFledglings = nFledglings.init)
prepbirds <- nimbleModel(code =fakenim, constants = myconsts,
                         data = mydat, inits = inits, calculate = T, check = T) #goes fast w/ fake data :)
prepbirds$calculate()
adaptInterval = 200
SamplerScale <- 0.75
mcmcbirds <- configureMCMC(prepbirds, monitors = c("alpha0", "alpha1"), print = T, control = list(adaptInterval = adaptInterval, scale=.1))

mcmcbirds$removeSampler(c("nFledglings"))
mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = c("nFledglings"), control =  list(M = 50, nocc = 3, Nt = c(10,3,5)),
                     type = "myfakeSampler", silent = F)

birdsMCMC <- buildMCMC(mcmcbirds)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(prepbirds) #takes a long time (sometimes)
Compbirds <- compileNimble(birdsMCMC, project = prepbirds) ### This throws the error
Compbirds$run(niter = 10, nburnin = 0, thin = 1, reset = F)

On Saturday, August 5, 2023 at 7:00:07 AM UTC-4 Daniel Turek wrote:
Heather, I admit offhand I don't see what's going wrong with your code.  Use of 

x <- rpois(1, lambda)

should work fine in compiled code (e.g., inside the run function of a custom-written MCMC sampler).

Is it possible for you to distill this down to a (minimal) reproducible example, which I can run to recreate the error?  If you would prefer to send that directly (off list) to avoid distributing details of your sampler or model code, that's fine as well.

Thanks,
Daniel
